channel.title: Weekly Digest
channel.description: The week's main stories from your sources

item.title: Experts warn of AI risks as global regulation debates intensify
item.description: Industry leaders and researchers are raising concerns about the potential dangers of advanced AI, calling for careful governance. While some argue for continued development, others warn of the risks posed by unchecked innovation and misuse. Why it matters: The debate over AI regulation highlights growing concerns about the technology's impact on society and the global balance of power. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Al Jazeera, Ara, BBC World, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Catalan leader honors Extremaduran contributions ahead of National Day
item.description: Salvador Illa visited Extremadura to celebrate the National Day of Catalonia, emphasizing the region's role in its development. Tensions remain over funding and migration between Catalonia and Spain, with Illa and regional leaders exchanging accusations. Why it matters: The event highlights ongoing political and cultural ties between Catalonia and Extremadura, with implications for regional identity and national policy. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, El Salto, La Directa, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Audiencia Nacional rechaza suspensión del campamento migratorio en Ceuta
item.description: La Audiencia Nacional ha negado la medida cautelar solicitada por el sindicato policial para suspender la instalación del campamento en Ceuta. El Parlamento Europeo ha aprobado una resolución de apoyo a la ciudad autónoma, aunque sin el respaldo de la izquierda. Why it matters: La decisión refleja la tensión entre la gestión migratoria y las protestas internas y externas al respecto. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Sweden's center-left narrowly wins election, far right loses ground
item.description: Sweden's center-left opposition narrowly won the election, edging out the ruling right-wing bloc. The far right party suffered its first defeat since entering parliament in 2010, while the Social Democrats recorded their worst result in a century. Why it matters: The election outcome could reshape Sweden's political landscape, with the center-left forming a new government and the far right facing its first electoral loss. (Sources: Al Jazeera, Ara, BBC World, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, RTVE, The Guardian World, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Supreme Court rejects amnesty for Puigdemont over corruption charges
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected a request by Puigdemont and Comín to apply an amnesty for corruption charges, despite a European Court ruling. The court cited concerns over financial interests of the EU and the need for constitutional guidance. Why it matters: This decision highlights ongoing legal tensions between national and European judicial interpretations of corruption charges. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Canada and EU Explore Closer Partnership Amid Global Tensions
item.description: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has called for a deeper alliance with the EU to strengthen collective resilience against global challenges. The proposal comes amid rising tensions with the U.S. and a shift in international power dynamics. While details remain unclear, the move signals a strategic realignment. Why it matters: This potential partnership could reshape diplomatic and economic strategies in a shifting global order. (Sources: 3Cat (324), Al Jazeera, Ara, El País, La Vanguardia, Público, RTVE, VilaWeb, eldiario.es)

item.title: Torrential rains cause floods and one death in Spain
item.description: Heavy rainfall across eastern Spain led to severe flooding, transport disruptions, and one fatality. Emergency services recovered a body in Barcelona after a vehicle was swept away by floodwaters. Weather forecasts indicate continued rain but with reduced intensity. Why it matters: The incident highlights the destructive power of extreme weather and its impact on daily life and infrastructure. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, La Vanguardia, Nació Digital, Público, RAC1, RTVE, VilaWeb)

item.title: Supreme Court Blocks Voting Rights for Spanish Nationals Abroad Under 'Nephew Law'
item.description: The Spanish Supreme Court has temporarily suspended the voting rights of Spanish nationals living abroad who obtained citizenship through the 'Nephew Law.' The decision has sparked political tensions, with the government and opposition parties expressing strong reactions. The law, aimed at granting citizenship to descendants of Franco-era victims, faces legal and political scrutiny. Why it matters: The ruling could reshape Spain's approach to citizenship and voting rights for diaspora communities, with broader implications for democratic participation and historical reconciliation. (Sources: 20minutos, 3Cat (324), Ara, El País, La Vanguardia, Público, RTVE, eldiario.es)
